prompt:
Make a narrow professional polish pass on the attached selected TVR Works website concept. This image is the EXACT visual target, not a moodboard. Preserve the established visual design, same near-black graphite surface, fine blue circular drafting geometry, crisp white typography, cyan diagram nodes, compact TVR monogram plus only "Works", centered hero, primary button and diagram structure. Do not invent a different site or additional sections. One independent full-page desktop website screenshot, no browser chrome, no collage, no device mockup.
Target dimensions: same desktop width as attached, approximately 1058px wide and a natural page height around 1540px. Preserve natural type proportions; reflow content and spacing rather than stretch or squash. The goal is a clean single-page professional-services website, ultimately to be implemented with React/shadcn/Base UI, but no technology implementation details should appear in the UI.
EXACT CHANGE A — AI BRANCH:
Replace the upper-right diagram heading "Build with AI" with exact heading "Put AI to work".
Replace its supporting line with EXACT "Insight, action & automation".
Keep this label in precisely the same upper-right quadrant with well-balanced spacing, same type style and hierarchy. Do not use AI-native or AI-enhanced elsewhere as replacement filler.
PROTECT ALL OTHER HERO AND DIAGRAM CONTENT:
Header: actual TVR monogram followed ONLY by "Works", plus white "Let's talk" button top right. No navigation.
Headline "Your vision." / "A partner to build it."
Hero copy "Turn a new idea into working software. Reimagine an existing system. Work directly with an engineer who brings product perspective and technical depth."
Hero white CTA "Let's talk".
Center circle ONLY says "One direct partnership" in balanced white type. No "You + Tim".
Other branch headings and supporting lines remain unchanged: "Create something new" with "Ideas → applications & solutions"; "Modernize what exists" with "Rebuild, integrate, improve"; "Get technical direction" with "Fractional leadership & advice".
Keep beautiful diagram fine white curved connectors, thin central circle, cyan joining dots, and subtle blue drafting circles. Adjust only very slightly for optical balance if needed.
EXACT CHANGE B — MAKE THE PERSONAL SECTION A DELIBERATE, WELL-BALANCED CLOSE:
The lower "Product perspective. Engineering depth." section must feel editorial and resolved, not a bordered intermediate panel ending in a detached footer.
Remove the vertical divider between heading and bio.
Soften the full-width horizontal line above this section to a very subtle low-contrast hairline, or remove it if spacing alone creates enough separation.
Retain the same two-column layout with generous gap. Left heading exact "Product perspective. Engineering depth.", same four-line stacked character as reference but about 8% smaller for a calmer relationship to the biography.
Give this final section equal generous breathing room above and below, approximately 85-100px at this image width. Align the top of right biography with the left heading. Avoid leaving a large empty tail or crowding the final lines.
Right column uses these EXACT short paragraphs, in this order:
"I'm Tim VanReenen. My background spans software engineering, product design, product management, and technical leadership."
"Applications and cloud infrastructure, built on the platforms that fit your business—including Azure and Google Cloud."
"Direct engagements and consulting partnerships."
"Whether you're exploring an idea or ready to build, I can help bring it to life."
Visually subordinate the direct-engagements sentence a little. Keep all paragraphs concise, comfortably readable and comfortably spaced. The final meaningful sentence is collaborative and inviting, not a cloud-provider list.
Place two quiet contact text links "Email ↗" and "LinkedIn ↗" directly below the final paragraph in the right column, with generous but connected spacing. Use restrained cyan for these links, not a giant CTA button or new slogan. These are integrated into the personal section.
Remove the entire separate footer band and its bright horizontal rule. Remove repeated footer "Tim VanReenen · Engineer & architect". Keep only a small muted "TVR Works LLC" at lower left, optically aligned with the integrated contact links to the right, within the same closing composition. No new headline, copyright block, legal inventory, social icon pile, repeated Let's talk CTA, or "A clear conversation..." section.
The final result should feel confident, personal, precise and finished. Preserve the selected design's restraint. No card grid, no faux dashboards, no stock people, no portraits, no client names, no invented metrics, no duplicate TVR wordmark, no extra decoration or new content. Check legibility, even optical weight, typography, negative space, connector alignment and a considered finish at the bottom.
